title: CI golden sync and weighted workload sampler for kernel/runtime benchmarks
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Introduce a deterministic golden-sync system and a weighted workload sampler to improve CI perf gate reliability across kernel-selection, attention-optimized kernels, and prefill/decode scheduling changes. The ticket covers orchestration logic, golden artifact reconciliation, and a lightweight sampler that maps production traces to deterministic synthetic mixes for repeatable CI runs. Motivation: CI flakes on perf gates are increasing because small changes in workload mix or stochastic scheduling lead to noisy baselines. We need a reproducible pipeline that (1) keeps goldens in sync with production-representative mixes, (2) prioritizes examples that are sensitive to kernel-switching and attention path changes, and (3) surfaces regressions with high signal-to-noise for engineer triage.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic golden artifacts produced and stored in S3 with content-addressed keys and metadata (model, kernel-profile, sequence distribution, seed).
Weighted workload sampler that generates CI trace mixes; sampling reproducible given seed and version; default seed stored in release metadata.
CI perf gate can run full golden comparison in under 30m for fast lanes and under 120m for extended lanes, with configurable sample size.
Regression signal precision >= 85% and false-positive rate <= 7% on historical validation suite over the last 12 weeks of production traces.
Dashboard tile in Console showing golden comparison trends, top failing examples, and attribution to kernel/attention/prefill scheduling changes.
Automated Slack alert + ticket template created for any perf gate fail with links to failing traces, CI artifacts, and suggested rollback policy.
tasks: Design golden artifact schema (metadata fields for kernel selection, attention optimizations, prefill/decode config, seed and workload mix)
Implement sampler service: ingest trace corpus, compute weighted selection by sensitivity score, export deterministic mix files
Add golden reconciliation job: compare new golden runs to stored baselines and compute delta metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, token-cost, kernel-utilization)
Integrate with CI: add fast lane (sample=200) and extended lane (sample=2k) jobs; implement gating thresholds and noise-aware z-score comparison
Produce Console dashboard and CI run artifacts uploader; hook up Slack alerts and linear ticket automation
Run historical backtest: validate thresholds and sampler weights using last 12 weeks of traces; document false-positive/negative rates
technical_notes: Sampler weighting heuristic: combine 1) trace frequency, 2) kernel-change sensitivity (from KR profiler), and 3) sequence-length tail mass to prioritize long-prefill scenarios.
Deterministic sampling requires a stable corpus ingest order and single random seed per run; any change to corpus must bump corpus-version in golden metadata.
Comparison metric: compute per-example latency deltas, normalized token-cost delta, and kernel-switch attribution; report aggregated p50/p90/p99 with confidence intervals via bootstrap.
CI optimization: fast lane uses pre-quantized models and cached KV prefill to reduce runtime; extended lane runs full-precision to catch regressions from kernel changes.
risks: Corpus drift: sampler weights need periodic recalibration to avoid under-sampling new production patterns.
Storage costs: content-addressed artifacts multiply storage needs; must implement TTL and pruning policy.
CI runtime variance: hardware differences between CI runners and perf labs could still introduce noise; mitigate with calibration runs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): implement artifact schema + sampler service MVP; run locally against archived traces
Phase 2 (week 3): integrate fast-lane CI job; run smoke tests and add soft alerts (no automatic blockers)
Phase 3 (week 4): enable extended lane and hard perf gates for kernel-routing and prefill scheduling PRs; monitor backtest metrics
Phase 4 (week 6): fully automate pruning, add console tile, and enable Slack automation for regression triage
